section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the Ten Days of Repentance parallel Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur, with the intermediate days drawing down influence for each corresponding day of the year, and the repentance of "Shuva Yisrael" encompassing both the elevation and drawing down of Atzmus Ein Sof.
section.t: And this is what [happens] during the Ten Days of Repentance
(the ten days between Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur)
the haftarah is "Shuva Yisrael ad Hashem Elokecha,"
for these days between Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur are analogous to Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur.

Therefore, just as Rosh Hashanah is the aspect of "head" from which life-force is drawn for all the days of the year, and also afterward the conduct throughout all the days of the year is according to the manner of conduct and decision of Rosh Hashanah
(as explained at length in Ateres Rosh B'Rosho),
and likewise Yom Kippur is also called by the name "Rosh Hashanah"75
and moreover, Yom Kippur is the aspect of soul and inwardness,76
similarly, regarding the seven days between Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur, they are the aspect of "head" from which [influence] is drawn to all the days of the year.
And in the manner found in the writings of the AriZal
(as above in section 1),
it can be said likewise77
that from the first day of the week within these seven days, influence is drawn to every first day throughout the year,
and from the second day of these seven days to every second day, etc.,
and from Shabbos Teshuvah to all the Shabbosos of the year.
Therefore, analogous to the two matters of elevation and drawing down in the shofar of Rosh Hashanah and in the recitation of the seven verses of "Hashem Hu HaElokim" at the conclusion of Yom Kippur,
so too is it with the repentance during the days of repentance between them
[and particularly on Shabbos Teshuvah,
the head of all the Shabbosos of the year,
Shabbos being the letters of "teshuv" (you shall return)],
that it contains these two matters.
And therefore we then say "Shuva Yisrael ad Hashem Elokecha,"
which includes both matters,
the elevation of the aspect of Yisrael
(Zeir Anpin)
and the aspect of "ad"
(Malchus)
to the aspect of "Hashem Elokecha," that is, to the Atzmus of Ein Sof, relative to Whom "Hashem" is considered like "Elokim,"
and afterward the drawing down from the Atzmus of Ein Sof to the aspect of "Hashem Elokecha," that is, to the aspect of Hashem as He becomes "your God," your strength and life-force.
And all this is accomplished through "Shuva" (return) without qualification,
the repentance that stems from the essence of the soul,
the turning back of the Yechidah
[and from this is drawn repentance in the aspect of Yisrael, the head of the soul, down to the foot of the soul],
and through this is accomplished the redemption from exile,
the individual redemption,78
and afterward also the general redemption with the coming of Moshiach Tzidkeinu, who comes to bring the righteous back in repentance,79
which also pertains to the aspect of Yechidah, as is known that Moshiach is the aspect of Yechidah,80
that it will be "He has redeemed my soul in peace... He has redeemed me and my children from among the nations,"81
in the true and complete redemption through Moshiach Tzidkeinu,
speedily, literally, and in our time.
